collected: From 10 real Brisbane job ads, collected from Seek in September 2026
headlineCap: ads required a finished IT qualification. Every single one said "or equivalent experience".

terms.plain: Employers have to check that your visa lets you do the job. Student visas, graduate visas and permanent residency all allow different things. Look up your own visa conditions before you decide you can't apply. Many people rule themselves out when they didn't need to.
This means no limit on your hours. A student visa usually has a limit, so this wording may not fit you. But not every job that says it actually needs it, so it can be worth asking.
A document that shows whether you have a criminal record. You apply online, pay a fee, and wait. It can take a few days or a few weeks. Some employers want one issued in the last three months.
Required in Queensland for any job where you might be around people under 18. You apply through the state government. It takes weeks, so start it early if you're looking at schools or youth services.
Two people who can speak about your work. A manager, a supervisor, or a lecturer if you haven't worked yet. Ask them first. Don't put someone's number down without checking.

Essential means you need it. Desirable, preferred, advantageous, or "bonus points" all mean the same thing: nice to have, not required. If you have the essentials, apply. Missing a desirable is normal.

How hard the problem is. Level 1 is passwords, printers, common issues. Level 2 is more complex. If you can't fix something you pass it up, which is called escalating. Nobody expects you to solve everything.
When someone has a problem they log a request, called a ticket. You pick it up, fix it, and write down what you did. Most IT jobs run this way.
The everyday work tools most Australian offices use: Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint. If you've used them as a student you already know more than you think.
Microsoft's tool for controlling who can log in to what. It used to be called Azure Active Directory, so you'll see both names. You'd use it to set up accounts for new staff.

Short IT qualifications you study for and sit an exam. They cost a few hundred dollars. Nine of these ten ads mentioned one, but only one actually required it, and several employers said they'd pay for yours after you start.
A company that runs IT for other businesses. You'd support many different clients instead of one employer. Good for learning fast.
Retirement money your employer pays on top of your salary. When an ad says "$70,000 + super", the super is extra, not part of the number.
Casual means no set hours and no paid leave, but a higher hourly rate. Part time and full time have set hours and paid leave. Check which one an ad is before applying.
Some charities and not-for-profits can pay part of your salary before tax, so you keep more of it. One of these ads offered up to $15,900 that way. It's a real benefit worth understanding.
A fixed pay scale set for the whole organisation. If an ad mentions one, the salary is usually not negotiable. The level tells you where you'd sit on the scale.
You take turns being contactable outside normal hours in case something breaks. Some jobs have it, some say clearly that they don't.
Some days in the office, some at home. Check which days are required. One of these ads asked for Monday, Tuesday and Thursday in the office.

mustHave.item: Being able to work through a problem
mustHave.note: The only thing all ten ads asked for. Not a qualification, a way of thinking.

mustHave.item: Explaining things clearly to non-technical people
mustHave.note: Asked for more often than any technical skill. Being patient counts.
Check your own visa conditions before you rule yourself out.
Outlook, Teams, OneDrive. If you've used them at uni, that counts.
Half the ads. Some also want you to have your own car.
Called documentation. Treated as a real skill, not paperwork.
Education and government employers. Apply early, it can take weeks.

niceToHave.note: Mentioned in nine ads. Required in one. Several employers offered to pay for yours.
Not one ad made it compulsory. Every single one said "or equivalent experience".
Firewalls, routing, VLANs. Always in the bonus list, never essential.
Helpful, never required, even for the systems administrator role.
Nice to have. Not having it doesn't stop you applying.
Fitness, education, telecoms. Explicitly described as not essential.

getReady.item: Blue Card, if you're looking at schools or youth work
getReady.why: The longest wait of anything here. Apply through the Queensland government before you start applying for those jobs, not after.
You apply and pay for it yourself. Some employers want one issued in the last three months, so don't get it too early either.

getReady.time: Months, if you don't have one
getReady.why: Five of ten ads wanted it. If you don't have an Australian licence yet, aim at the other five for now and start the process.
Message them now and ask permission. A lecturer or a manager from part-time work is fine. Have their name, role, phone and email ready.

getReady.item: An entry-level certificate like AZ-900 or MS-900
getReady.time: One to two weeks of study
getReady.why: Online, affordable, and it appears in nine of these ten ads. Not required anywhere, but it's the quickest way to look serious if you have no experience yet.

getReady.item: One story about a problem you solved
getReady.why: Write down what broke, what you did, and what changed. One ad asked for exactly this. It also comes up in almost every interview.

getReady.item: Check what your visa actually allows
getReady.why: Nine of ten ads ask about work rights. Know your exact answer so you apply with confidence instead of guessing.
